source: Alavi Naeini et al. (2023) Large Language Models are Fixated by Red Herrings (Only Connect Wall)
finding: Built the OCW dataset from a quiz-show wall task with deliberate red-herring groups. LLMs and embeddings fail far below humans, and the authors read this as an Einstellung-like fixation.
numbers: Humans solved 285 of 494 walls (1405 of 1976 groups). Best static embedding (E5-base) solved 1 wall, 89 correct groups. All other embeddings solved 0.
limits: Human numbers are from the show's contestants, not a controlled lab sample. The Einstellung link is argued, not measured with a fixation-then-release design.
agent_relevance: A hard-to-ignore distractor group is a standard failure for S6 operator choice; test the schema on trap items.

source: Alavi Naeini et al. (2023) Large Language Models are Fixated by Red Herrings (Only Connect Wall) - GPT-3.5/GPT-4 few-shot
finding: GPT-4 with in-context examples was over 2x the best embedding in correct groups but still solved almost no full walls.
numbers: GPT-4 solved 2 to 7 walls of 494 (about 1%) with 0 to 10 shots, 137 to 269 correct groups. GPT-3.5 solved 0 walls, 114 to 140 correct groups. Humans 285 walls.
limits: The extracted results table was garbled; per-shot cells read approximately. Early 2023 models only.
agent_relevance: Few-shot examples barely help on fixation-style tasks; do not count on in-context examples to break set.

source: Alavi Naeini et al. (2023) Large Language Models are Fixated by Red Herrings (Only Connect Wall) - red-herring ablation
finding: Removing or diluting red herrings raised LLM performance sharply, supporting the red-herring retrieval hypothesis (strong distractors cause negative transfer).
numbers: GPT-4 solved up to about 68 walls on OCW-Randomized and roughly 280 to 470 on OCW-WordNet (no red herrings), versus 2 to 7 on original OCW. GPT-3.5 rose from 0 to 5-17 and 279-471.
limits: Synthetic variants also change difficulty in other ways (WordNet groups are easier), so the gain is not purely red-herring removal. Cell-to-model mapping in the garbled table is approximate.
agent_relevance: Gives a test design: same items with and without a planted attractor, to measure fixation cost for a scaffold.

source: Hao, Alexandre, Yu (2025) Visual LLMs Exhibit Human-Level Cognitive Flexibility in the WCST
finding: WCST-64 on GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5 Pro, Claude-3.5 Sonnet in a 2x2: visual vs text input, straight-to-answer vs chain of thought. Set-shifting was near random without CoT and matched or beat humans with CoT on text.
numbers: Claude-3.5 Sonnet CoT-text: 5.00 categories completed (SD 0), correct-learning rate about 67.5%. Straight-answer cells for other models: 0.1 to 0.5 categories and 25-40 non-perseverative errors (near chance). Human row: about 4.7 categories, 65% (row mapping approximate, table garbled). 10 runs per cell.
limits: 10 runs per model per cell; 64 trials; small human sample; visual input much worse (visual recognition issues).
agent_relevance: Explicit reasoning before the rule-switch decision gives flexibility. A step that states the current hypothesis then checks feedback is needed in S6.
quote: VLLMs achieve or surpass human-level set-shifting capabilities under chain-of-thought prompting with text-based inputs

source: Hao et al. (2025) WCST - role-play impairment
finding: With role-play prompts, models can imitate patients with set-shifting or inhibitory deficits, with more perseverative or non-perseverative errors.
numbers: One model's non-perseverative errors rose from 3.50 to 20.10 under the most severe impairment prompt; an inhibitory-control prompt gave PE 12.80, NPE 18.70 in another.
limits: Simulating a deficit does not show the model has a brain-like architecture; that claim is speculative.
agent_relevance: Flexibility can be shifted by prompt framing alone, so persona text in a scaffold matters.

source: Li, Zhang, Holme, Hu, Wang (2025) LLMs are Near-Optimal Decision-Makers with a Non-Human Learning Behavior
finding: Five LLMs (GPT-4o, o4-mini, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek) versus 360 new human participants on WCST, Iowa and Cambridge gambling. In WCST, LLMs beat humans except DeepSeek and approach an optimal strategy.
numbers: 360 humans (mean age 18.95). WCST: all LLMs except DeepSeek had more correct matches than humans and needed fewer trials to finish set 1; failure-to-maintain-set comparable to humans. Gemini and o4-mini highest median correct.
limits: Young student human sample; exact LLM run counts not extracted.
agent_relevance: Strong models are not rigid on simple rule change; the risk is elsewhere (prior-driven answers on rich tasks).

source: Li, Zhang, Holme, Hu, Wang (2025) LLMs are Near-Optimal Decision-Makers with a Non-Human Learning Behavior - error type
finding: Error pattern differs: humans made more non-perseverative (random) errors than perseverative; LLMs except DeepSeek made more perseverative errors than non-perseverative. LLM mistakes are sticking to the old rule, not noise.
numbers: Direction only in main text; statistics in SI Table S3. 15 prompt variants of WCST x 10 repeats with GPT-4o left the pattern qualitatively unchanged.
limits: With few random errors, a small number of perseverations dominates.
agent_relevance: When an LLM errs after a context switch, suspect a stale set; S6 should check against the previous operator.

source: Li et al. (2025) - cognitive modeling of the tasks
finding: Fitted learning models show LLMs learn from reward and punishment differently from humans (higher learning rate in Iowa; stronger penalty reactions except GPT). Hence near-optimal but non-human.
numbers: All five LLMs had higher learning rates than humans in the Iowa task (Mann-Whitney). WCST reward and punishment sensitivity estimated by Bayesian model (SI).
limits: Model fit is to a human-designed model; fit does not prove mechanism.
agent_relevance: Do not assume human flexibility theory transfers parameter by parameter.

source: Li et al. (2024) Reflection-Bench: Evaluating Epistemic Agency in LLMs
finding: Seven cognitive tasks including WCST across many models and prompt strategies (44 model-strategy pairs). Reasoning models and zero-shot CoT help some tasks but not all.
numbers: WCST (72 trials, 6 rule blocks): o1-preview and Claude-3.5-Sonnet both 81.25, Gemini-1.5-pro 64.58. Cross-model accuracy by block: shape 80.0%, color 44.2%, number 26.0%, shape 76.4%, color 47.0%, number 45.4%.
limits: Rule order fixed (shape-color-number), so the first block is confounded. Scores vary by prompt strategy. Author list not verified.
agent_relevance: Accuracy dips after each rule change and recovers slowly: a measurable perseveration cost to use as a regression test.

source: Li et al. (2024) Reflection-Bench: Evaluating Epistemic Agency in LLMs - overall
finding: Claude-3.5-Sonnet topped entry-level difficulty, then o1-preview and DeepSeek-Reasoner; extended reasoning is not uniformly better (direct generation sometimes scores higher).
numbers: Claude-3.5-Sonnet 68.78 (zero-shot CoT) and 68.23 (free output); o1-preview 66.57 (direct), 64.94 (free output); DeepSeek-Reasoner 64.56 / 61.47; o1-mini 58.64 / 54.29.
limits: Aggregate over tasks; no human baseline.
agent_relevance: Longer reasoning does not by itself guarantee adaptivity.

source: Kim et al. (2025) Limitations of LLMs in Clinical Problem-Solving Arising from Inflexible Reasoning (M-ARC)
finding: M-ARC: 100 hand-written medical questions that alter a familiar pattern so the stock answer is wrong (Einstellung design). Most LLMs under 50%; best below physicians.
numbers: 5 physicians averaged 66% (SE 5.3%). Best: Gemini 1.5 Pro 50%, o1 48%. Several models near or below 20% chance. Larger models within a family tend to do better.
limits: Only 100 items, 5 humans, written by the authors; items unlikely in real life; humans also fall for the trap. Later published in Scientific Reports (Nov 2025).
agent_relevance: Closest direct test of expert-style flexibility in LLMs; an operator asking what in this case breaks the usual pattern belongs in S6.
quote: LLMs exhibit overconfidence in their answers, despite their limited accuracy

source: Kim et al. (2025) M-ARC - calibration
finding: Agreement- and entropy-based self-consistency Brier scores show overconfidence in the top models (o1, Gemini-pro, Claude-opus, Llama-3.1-70b); smaller models are more overconfident.
numbers: Reliability plots show confidence above accuracy; larger models better calibrated but still overconfident.
limits: Exact Brier values are in figures, not extracted.
agent_relevance: Agreement between samples is not a safe stop signal; a fixation trap yields consistent wrong answers.

source: Chen et al. (2026) MedEinst: Benchmarking the Einstellung Effect in Medical LLMs
finding: 5,383 paired clinical cases over 49 diseases: a control case plus a trap case where altered evidence flips the diagnosis. Bias Trap Rate = chance of misdiagnosing the trap while getting the control right. Frontier models are accurate yet fall into traps.
numbers: 17 LLMs tested. Gemini-2.5-Pro Bias Trap Rate 60.90%. Frontier models above 50%. Robust accuracy for most models about 11-12%. Physician review: 96.1% of pairs judged valid.
limits: Pairs built partly with LLM-as-judge; the results table in the text was garbled so some model-to-number mapping is uncertain; authors also propose their own agent.
agent_relevance: A paired control/trap design is a template for measuring operator switching in our agent.

source: Chen et al. (2026) MedEinst: Benchmarking the Einstellung Effect in Medical LLMs - failure modes
finding: Error analysis of GPT-5: blindness, then underthinking, then overthinking.
numbers: 35% of GPT-5 error cases ignore key discriminative evidence (blindness); of cases where evidence was noticed, 43% underthinking and 22% overthinking (rationalising the wrong prior).
limits: Single model, qualitative coding.
agent_relevance: Three failure types suggest different fixes: attention to anomalies, depth, anti-rationalisation.

source: Chen et al. (2026) MedEinst: Benchmarking the Einstellung Effect in Medical LLMs - scaling and agents
finding: No meaningful link between model size and robustness; stronger models have higher baseline accuracy and a higher trap rate ('stronger priors, stronger blindness'). Debate-style multi-agent frameworks reinforce the dominant prior.
numbers: MDAgent (debate) trap rate 40.34%, robust accuracy 3.20%; DyLAN 41.69%, 1.19% on Qwen3-32B. Qwen3-32B base accuracy 40.25%.
limits: Scaling claim is cross-family and correlational. Authors' own comparison.
agent_relevance: Debate or voting among copies of one model will not cure fixation; argues against naive multi-agent voting.

source: Chen et al. (2026) MedEinst: Benchmarking the Einstellung Effect in Medical LLMs - ECR-Agent fix
finding: A structured scaffold (dual-pathway perception, causal graph of discriminative evidence, evidence audit, memory of validated paths) cut the trap rate.
numbers: Qwen3-32B: base accuracy 40.25% to 55.49% with Dynamic Causal Inference, to 69.49% with memory; final trap rate 33.75%, robust accuracy 24.21%.
limits: Authors' own method on their own benchmark; source code announced, not released.
agent_relevance: Evidence a scaffold can help: list discriminating features of rival hypotheses before answering.

source: Haq et al. (2025) Is your LLM trapped in a Mental Set?
finding: Short study adapting DeCaro (2016) math-equivalence tasks (complex vs shortcut strategy, problem order) to Llama-3.1-8B/70B and GPT-4o. CoT raised accuracy but made models use more steps than the humans' one-step shortcut.
numbers: Six problems per condition only. GPT-4o exact match with few-shot: shortcut 0.33, shortcut after complex 0.66, complex 0.66, complex after shortcut 0.83. With few-shot plus zero-shot CoT every model solved in 3 steps.
limits: Tiny N, no statistics, no humans run; the mental-set claim rests on step count. Weak evidence.
agent_relevance: Order effects may exist but evidence is thin; a powered Luchins replication on LLMs is a gap.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Reasoning Strategies in LLMs: Can They Follow, Prefer, and Optimize?
finding: Models can be told to follow one of four strategies (supposition following, chain construction, compound, concatenation), but no single strategy wins and the model cannot pick the best one itself. An oracle picking per problem gains a lot.
numbers: TruthQuest (2,400 questions): no-strategy Phi-4 47.2%, R1-Distill 63.4%; oracle 82.9% and 90.1%. ZebraLogic: Qwen3 32.0% vs oracle 36.4%. Majority vote over strategies: Phi-4 54.9%, R1-Distill 68.4%; verifier 74.1% for R1-Distill.
limits: Small open models (7B-14B). Logic puzzles only. Final-answer accuracy only.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence for S6: LLMs lack adaptive strategy choice, but running several operators and verifying beats letting the model choose. Ensemble-with-check is the practical route.
quote: no single strategy consistently improves accuracy

source: Mondorf and Plank (2024) as reported in Zhang et al. 2025
finding: Earlier manual analysis found each LLM defaults to one preferred strategy on logical deduction. Zhang et al. report one model used supposition following in about 60% of cases while Llama-2-70B favored chain construction.
numbers: About 60% for one model (model name not extracted).
limits: Secondhand; the original paper not opened.
agent_relevance: Models have habitual strategies, analogous to einstellung toward a trained method.

source: Sui et al. (2025/2026) Meta-Reasoner: Dynamic Guidance for Optimized Inference-time Reasoning
finding: A meta layer reads progress reports and picks, via a contextual bandit, whether to continue, backtrack, switch strategy or restart. It beats baselines on Game of 24, TheoremQA and SciBench and cuts time.
numbers: Game of 24 GPT-4o-mini: CoT 4%, ToT(b=5) 65%, MACM 80%, Meta-Reasoner 89%; GPT-4o 92%. TheoremQA GPT-4o-mini 84.13% vs MACM-with-GPT-4-Turbo 79.41%. Time down 28-35% vs search methods.
limits: Authors' own method; reward uses an LLM judge; version 6 (May 2026) numbers differ from earlier versions; baselines taken from other papers.
agent_relevance: Closest working analogue of adaptive expertise inside an agent loop: monitor progress, then switch operator.

source: Meta-Reasoner ablation
finding: Dynamic strategy set beats fixed sets; dropping the bandit (asking the LLM which strategy to use) hurts more than dropping progress summaries.
numbers: Fixed K=3: 65% Game of 24, 72.34% TheoremQA; K=5: 72%, 79.17%; dynamic 89%, 84.13% (14 and 21 unique strategies).
limits: GPT-4o-mini only.
agent_relevance: Self-chosen strategy by free prompting is weak; supports an explicit selection rule.

source: Bogdan (2026) Free Energy Heuristics: Fast-and-Frugal Cognition as Active Inference
finding: Pre-registered study of 7 models on 79 Knightian-uncertainty frames: longer chain of thought lowers accuracy when meta-uncertainty is high (a less-is-more effect, tied to take-the-best), but not on matched controls.
numbers: 7 models (5 open 3B-32B, 2 frontier), 5 CoT lengths, 7,875 responses. Posterior median accuracy drop 17.3 points (95% CrI 7.7 to 25.5) in the high-uncertainty regime. Decisive in mid-to-large models, directional in frontier, absent-to-reversed in the two weakest.
limits: Single-author preprint, not peer reviewed; benchmark built by the author; regime defined by a variance score.
agent_relevance: Supports a switch rule: do not extend deliberation on questions with no checkable answer. Treat as hypothesis until replicated.

source: Bogdan (2026) - theory claim
finding: Claims that under heavy-tailed precision uncertainty the optimal policy truncates cue use after k cues, identical to take-the-best under Descending Dominance (Theorem 2.7.4).
numbers: Formal result; simulate-and-recover correlation above 0.96 for the regime score.
limits: Mathematical equivalence under stated conditions only.
agent_relevance: A formal bridge between the Gigerenzer toolbox and the agent's stop rule.

source: Gu and Shi (2025) Einstellung Rigidity Index in Continual Learning
finding: Not an LLM: defines an index of shortcut-induced rigidity (adaptation delay, performance deficit, reliance on suboptimal feature) in continual-learning networks, named after Einstellung.
numbers: Two-phase CIFAR-100 with a spurious magenta patch in phase 2; fine-tuning, online EWC and replay-type methods compared.
limits: Image classification, analogy only; authors advise using it as a conservative screen.
agent_relevance: Template metric: delay in adopting a better method after a prior method was rewarded.

source: Kennedy and Nowak (2024) WCST for LLMs, cited by Reflection-Bench
finding: Reflection-Bench states it implements WCST following Kennedy and Nowak (2024); original not opened.
limits: Cited only.
agent_relevance: Prior LLM WCST work exists.

source: Trapped by Expectations: Functional Fixedness in LLM-Enabled Chat Search (2025)
finding: Crowd study of 450 participants: earlier experience with other tools shapes prompts; when the chat system fails expectations they write longer, more varied prompts. It is about human fixation on the tool, not model fixation.
numbers: 450 participants (from search-listing gist).
limits: Only listing text read.
agent_relevance: User-side fixation can also hit the agent interface.

source: HybridMind (NeurIPS 2025) strategy selection
finding: Search snippet reports a fine-tuned LLaMA-3.1-8B meta-selector choosing between natural-language and symbolic reasoning beat GPT-4o natural-language reasoning by 4.4% on FOLIO and 1.3% on MATH.
numbers: +4.4% FOLIO, +1.3% MATH (secondary summary).
limits: Not opened; verify before use.
agent_relevance: Another per-problem strategy-selector result, consistent with Zhang et al.

source: arXiv title searches (Nov 2026): Einstellung, functional fixedness
finding: Title searches for Einstellung give only Alavi Naeini 2023, MedEinst 2026 and the ERI paper; for functional fixedness only a chat-search user study. Web searches found no LLM study of the Luchins jar task with reasoning models, and none testing whether LLMs pick among fast-and-frugal heuristics as people do.
numbers: 3 Einstellung-titled papers, 1 functional-fixedness paper at search time.
limits: Title searches only; papers using other words (mental set, rigidity) may be missed. OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and arXiv API were rate-limited this session.
agent_relevance: Gap: a powered Luchins-style test on current models is open work and could be run on our own agent.
